clue.text: Newspaper or clothing business

parts.note: a rag is slang both for a cheap newspaper and for a piece of clothing
trade means business or commerce

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone works in the press or in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG covers both 'newspaper' and 'clothing' at once, and TRADE is the business; together they name the garment industry.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is the informal name for the fashion and garment-making industry.

clue.text: Few benefit when it's drawn

parts.note: a lottery-style prize draw has many ticket buyers but only a few winners when the tickets are pulled out

explanation.surface: Only a handful gain when the draw is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' sounds like a sketch or a tie, but it means winning tickets drawn from a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a fundraising lottery whose prizes go to a few tickets drawn at random.

clue.text: Unwashed food put aside

parts.note: grub is informal for food
by means aside or to one side, as in put by

explanation.surface: Dirty food has been set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: GRUB (food) plus BY, as in 'put by', meaning set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty, grimy, not having been cleaned.

clue.text: Upset some salt while laying a snare

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: part means some of something
a tar or old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone spilt salt while setting a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like the seasoning; it is a sailor, TAR. 'Upset' turns PART TAR upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattrap is a device for catching rodents, a type of snare.

clue.text: Fraudulent practice gets two black marks

parts.note: double means twofold
a cross is a mark of error or disapproval

explanation.surface: Cheating earns a pair of demerits.
explanation.walkthrough: DOUBLE (two) plus CROSS (the mark against a wrong answer): two black marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-cross is a betrayal, deceiving an ally while pretending to cooperate.

clue.text: Seizes sovereign midst sounds of horror

indicators.note: midst means the sovereign's letter sits in the middle of the sounds of horror

parts.note: gasps are sharp breaths taken in shock or horror
R, for Rex or Regina, is the abbreviation for a reigning monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch grabs something amid cries of horror from onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midst' puts R inside GASPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to take hold of it firmly, to clutch it.

clue.text: Yields after shots by army corps

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
turns are goes or attempts, as in having a shot

explanation.surface: An army regiment produces results after firing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' suggests gunfire; it means goes or attempts, TURNS. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are profits or the yield from an investment.

clue.text: Sort of cut that's superficial

definitions.meaning: a wound only through the outer surface of the body
shallow, not going beneath the surface

explanation.definitionFit: A cut that only breaks the outer layer of the body is called this, and the phrase also means shallow or surface-level.

clue.text: Fed meals cooked by one's unaided efforts

indicators.note: cooked means tampered with or prepared, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fed meals prepared entirely by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges FED MEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-made person achieved success through their own work without help.

clue.text: As productive as a market-gardener?

parts.note: a grower of produce has a crop full of fruit, so the word for productive is read as 'full of fruit'

explanation.surface: Comparing someone's productivity to that of a vegetable grower.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: the word meaning productive splits into 'fruit' and 'full', just what a market-gardener's crop is.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitful means yielding good results, producing plenty.

clue.text: A time to make bequests as one wants

parts.note: to will is to leave property to someone in a will

explanation.surface: A suggestion that now is the moment to draw up bequests just as you please.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then T for time, then WILL, the verb for bequeathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever or however you please.

clue.text: Broad-minded and generous

definitions.meaning: tolerant and open to other views

explanation.definitionFit: Liberal means tolerant of other opinions, and also giving freely, as in a liberal helping.

clue.text: Lack of interest in bedroom refurbishment

indicators.note: refurbishing a room rearranges it, so the letters of bedroom are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has grown bored with the bedroom makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbishment' rearranges BEDROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weary state of feeling no interest in anything.

clue.text: Misjudgements about coach carrying gun

indicators.note: about means the misjudgements go around the coach

parts.note: blunders are careless mistakes
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: Errors involving a coach carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the misjudgements wrap round the coach. 'carrying' is only a link to the definition, the old gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunderbuss is an old short-barrelled firearm with a flared muzzle.

clue.text: Drive faster to collect a drug

parts.note: to pick up something is to collect it
speed is slang for amphetamine, a drug

explanation.surface: Instructions to hurry a car along to fetch some narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK UP (collect) plus SPEED (slang for amphetamine).
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up speed is to accelerate, to go more quickly.

clue.text: A us state, say, in hyped-up state

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida, a US state
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone in an American state is worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A, plus FL (Florida), plus UTTER (say).
explanation.definitionFit: Aflutter means nervously excited or agitated.

clue.text: Passing by naval force in Gateshead

parts.note: a fleet is a group of warships
taken as written
read as gate's head, the first letter of gate

explanation.surface: A navy goes by Gateshead, a town on the Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: Gateshead is a town in north-east England, but here it splits as 'gate's head', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means brief, transient, quickly gone.

clue.text: Vigorous thoroughbred

definitions.meaning: of unmixed breeding or pure pedigree

explanation.definitionFit: Full-blooded describes wholehearted vigour, and also an animal of pure, unmixed breeding.

clue.text: A pound returned to diner who complains

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is turned back

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
a diner is someone who eats

explanation.surface: A pound sent back to a diner who is moaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pound' is the weight abbreviation, and 'returned' turns it round; the diner then follows, and the definition is 'who complains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleater is someone who moans or grumbles, a whinger.

clue.text: Transport retired vicar to food store

parts.note: a deli or delicatessen sells food

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the title is reversed

parts.note: Rev, for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman is sent off to a grocery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the vicar's title back to front; it is put after the food store, with 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to carry goods to their destination.

clue.text: Two young men with elderly mother

parts.note: Mat is a short form of Matthew, a man's name
Ron is a short form of Ronald, a man's name

explanation.surface: Two lads accompany an older mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Two boys' names, MAT and RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a dignified, mature married woman.

clue.text: Tout told to get on his bike

indicators.note: told means the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to pedal is to work a bicycle

explanation.surface: A salesman is told to cycle off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on his bike' suggests 'go away'; it means PEDAL, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle is to sell goods by hawking them about.

clue.text: Vain appeal to wanton consumers

definitions.meaning: a plea to wasteful shoppers would be to cut back their consumption, split into two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: what you would urge on wasteful consumers is 'use less', which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless means futile, having no effect, as a vain effort does.

clue.text: About to get tenancy contract for free

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
a lease is a contract letting property to a tenant

explanation.surface: A landlord is about to sign a tenancy agreement for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) plus LEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone is to set them loose from captivity.

clue.text: Pole surrounded by idiots screws it up

indicators.note: surrounded by means the pole's letter goes inside the word for idiots

parts.note: twits are foolish people
S, for the South Pole, is one of the two poles

explanation.surface: A Polish man, encircled by fools, makes a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person; it is S, a magnetic or geographic pole. 'surrounded by' puts S inside TWITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisting something up is screwing or wringing it into a contorted shape.

clue.text: Shook when Eve and Rex somehow came into money

indicators.note: came into means the rearranged letters go inside the word for money

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling

indicators.note: somehow suggests an uncertain arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Two people trembled on inheriting a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges Eve plus R into VERE, and 'came into' sets that inside the money; quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver is to tremble or shake slightly, so quivered means trembled.

clue.text: Judge held in high esteem

explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something as good is to judge it so, and regard also means respect or esteem.

clue.text: Gents are crazy to cause disaffection

indicators.note: crazy suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Men behaving madly alienate people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GENTS ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, making someone unfriendly or distant.
